transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel, Daniel Cho, Priya Menon, Miguel Alvarez (Redwood) — Mark Thompson, Aisha Rahman, Liam O'Neill, Natalie Chen (CleverHealth)
Links shared: slides (redwood.com/decks/optimize-qprofiles), benchmark sheet (drive.google.com/…/cleverhealth-bench), perf runner repo (github.com/redwood/perf-runner)

00:00:12 Samira (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'll give a 2 minute agenda: quick context, then daniel will demo the optimize console and qprofile flow, then priya will show comparisons between int8 and fp8 on latency/quality, and we'll leave time for technical Qs.
00:00:26 Mark (CleverHealth): thanks, samira. we have a few specific goals — want predictable 50ms p95 across our chat completions and also cut token cost roughly 30% without degrading NPS.
00:00:40 Daniel (SE): got it. just to set expectations, INT8 and FP8 are different knobs — int8 tends to give higher throughput but can introduce quantization noise on certain layers; fp8 often hits better quality at slightly higher cost. we'll show real traces.
00:01:04 Aisha: quick infra note — we run in a customer VPC with private dedicated nodes; we'll need KMS integration and tenant isolation. can you confirm private deployment behavior?
00:01:20 Priya (Product): yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM, and the Optimize table in the console is identical across hosted and private. audit logs are shipped to your cloud SIEM if you enable the integration.
00:01:36 Natalie (Security): when you say audit logs, is the raw prompt included or just meta? we have PHI concerns.
00:01:45 Miguel: by default audit logs redact prompt text; we do provide a redaction mode toggle and an enterprise retention option. we'll send the SOC2 appendix after this call.
00:02:02 Mark: perfect. let's jump into the demo.
00:02:15 Daniel: switching to screen — Console > Optimize tab. you'll see qprofiles listed; each profile is a bundle: quantization type, per-layer overrides, per-sequence-length tuning, and batch heuristics. the UI lets you preview expected latency delta and estimated cost impact — those numbers come from our offline profiler.
00:03:05 (30s silence while screenshare loads)
00:03:40 Daniel: here is a sample QProfile we created for a 13B LLM — default INT8 global quant plus FP8 for attention and the final MLP. that mixed precision tends to keep logits stable while still getting most throughput wins.
00:04:10 Aisha: what does "global quant" mean — does it rewrite model weights or is this runtime quantization?
00:04:20 Daniel: good question — it's a compilation-time quantization step that writes a quantized artifact to disk (we call it a q-blob) which the runtime loads. per-layer overrides allow you to keep sensitive layers at higher precision. the runtime also supports on-the-fly cast for some kernels but we prefer the q-blob for consistency.
00:05:00 Mark: any compatibility issues with KV cache across these profiles? our chat stack relies heavily on KV cache for long contexts.
00:05:10 Priya: KV cache semantics are preserved; but some quantized kernels have slightly different memory layouts so cache hot paths are profiled separately. you might see a small p99 bump on very long contexts if the cache becomes fragmented — we have heuristics to compact.
00:05:45 Liam: are we talking about a 5–10% delta or something worse?
00:05:52 Daniel: typical p95 improvements for INT8 mixed configs are 1.8–2.5x throughput; latency can drop 30–50% depending on batch. p99 might suffer up to 10% without prefix caching. with prefix caching you'll recover most regressions.
00:06:30 Priya: switching to benchmark slides — here's the latency vs quality scatter for our 13B customer-like workload. X axis is average latency, Y axis is Rouge-L drop vs FP32 baseline (lower is better). INT8 mixed points cluster lower latency but have some outliers with >2.5% quality drop on niche prompts. FP8 points are near baseline quality but with moderate latency improvements.
00:07:10 Mark: can you show example prompts where int8 fails?
00:07:16 Priya: yes — we included prompts with math reasoning and tricky tokenization patterns. e.g., prompts with repeated special tokens and very deep attention patterns showed hallucination increase with pure INT8. the mixed-profile that keeps attention at fp8 mitigated that.
00:07:45 Natalie: that aligns with our safety reviews — hallucination uptick is a major red flag. is there an automated evaluation to surface regressions before rollout?
00:07:55 Miguel: Optimize supports eval hooks — you can associate a prompt set and baseline metric (BLEU, ROUGE, custom classifier). when we simulate a profile we run the eval and flag regressions beyond a threshold. it's in the console under "Quality checks".
00:08:22 Aisha: how long does a full eval take for, say, 5k prompts?
00:08:27 Daniel: depends on model/throughput — on a dedicated 8xA100 pool it's about 20–40 minutes for 5k prompts with streaming metrics. we'll provide a perf-runner script to reproduce.
00:08:45 Mark: ok. if we pick a mixed profile and go to production, what's the rollback story?
00:08:52 Priya: rollouts are handled at the route level. you can do canary (percent-based), A/B, or tag-based. automatic fallback policy can detect quality regressions in the first N requests and route back to baseline. the console shows projected cost/latency for the percent split.
00:09:24 Liam: does fallback incur additional cost due to double requests?
00:09:28 Miguel: fallback is a routing decision; we don't double-run by default. we route some percentage to new profile and monitor metrics. if it fails we switch the percentage back. some teams opt to run shadow requests to collect quality metrics — that does double cost.
00:09:48 Mark: can you remind us about mixed-batch behavior? our client uses variable prompt lengths.
00:09:55 Daniel: Redwood runtime uses continuous batching and workload-aware batching policies. shorter prompts get packed; the Optimize suggestions will recommend batch sizes and max-token thresholds. for mixed precision the kernel selection is dynamic: if a batch contains tokens requiring different per-layer precisions, the runtime can execute mixed-kernel sequences, but that can reduce throughput. our QProfile simulation models that.
00:10:32 Aisha: is the simulation accurate? we've seen mismatches elsewhere.
00:10:36 Priya: it's within +-10% for latency in our field tests; quality predictions are more conservative — we bias towards safety and will show worst-case quality drops. we'll attach the assumptions in the sheet.
00:10:50 (short cross-talk)
00:11:10 Daniel: demo time — create a new QProfile. name: ch-int8-fast, base: INT8 global, overrides: attention fp8, final MLP fp8, batch hint 64 tokens, prefix cache enabled. Apply to route preview. console shows p50 44ms (projected), cost -32% vs baseline, expected Rouge-L delta -0.9%.
00:12:05 Mark: interesting. can we pin this to only our staging route?
00:12:10 Daniel: yes — you can scope to environment, model version, or detection tag. you can also pin by API key.
00:12:20 Natalie: regarding PHI, since we want redaction — would QProfiles ever cause us to see raw prompt data in logs?
00:12:29 Miguel: not unless you enable full request logging; by default we keep metadata and hash tokens for metrics. redaction is enforced at the edge before any q-blob usage.
00:12:45 Aisha: how do we run our own bench — do you provide dockerized runner?
00:12:51 Daniel: yes — perf-runner repo is a docker image and a simple harness. it can replay traces at scale and output token-level latency histograms. we'll give you a sample config for your node types.
00:13:15 (demo pauses; attendees scanning sheet)
00:13:45 Priya: here's an interesting point — FP8 often gives you a sweet spot for attention-heavy models because attention matmuls benefit from higher dynamic range. INT8 gives bigger memory and compute wins for MLP-dominated sections. that's why mixed is common.
00:14:05 Mark: does Redwood provide automated suggestions for per-layer overrides?
00:14:10 Priya: yes — Optimize has a suggestion engine that runs per-model profiling and generates starter QProfiles with recommended per-layer exceptions. you can accept or tweak and re-run evals.
00:14:30 Liam: about caching — you mentioned prefix caching earlier. will that interact with memory footprint for quantized blobs?
00:14:37 Daniel: prefix caching is orthogonal — it's about token-level reuse. but the q-blob memory layout can affect L2 cache locality which changes p99 behavior. our heuristics detect when prefix caching would be particularly helpful and recommend it.
00:14:58 Natalie: any compliance docs we can review after? specifically KMS integration flow and redaction proofing.
00:15:05 Samira: yes, i'll send SOC2, ISO appendix, and a KMS integration guide. we'll mark the redaction section.
00:15:18 Mark: let's talk about quantization regression visibility — will we be able to tie quality regressions to specific prompts/persona? we need to triage quickly.
00:15:27 Miguel: yes — the evaluation dashboard allows you to filter by prompt tag, persona, or route. we also support quick diffs between model outputs with side-by-side highlighting. you can add custom metric hooks that run a classifier to surface hallucination.
00:15:50 Aisha: how are hallucinations detected? do you provide models for that?
00:15:55 Priya: we provide a default hallucination classifier and support webhooks to run your own model in your environment. many enterprise customers bring a lightweight instruction-following classifier.
00:16:12 (short pause)
00:16:30 Daniel: demoing the QProfile application — apply to 10% of traffic on staging. i'll show the rollout slider. the console predicts the expected token cost delta and shows the evaluation snapshots.
00:17:00 Mark: can we do automated rollback after N failures? how are failures defined?
00:17:05 Priya: failures are user-definable; defaults are increases in regression metric beyond threshold or p95 latency growth beyond threshold. you can set short-circuiting to 5 minutes or rolling window.
00:17:25 Liam: how do we measure quality in production? we don't have labels on live traffic.
00:17:30 Miguel: common approach is a hybrid: run a small percentage to new profile and send a copy to a labeling pipeline (manual or classifier). we also recommend synthetic prompts that are representative and periodically run them in production shadow mode.
00:18:00 Mark: what about sequence length extremes — our customers sometimes send 8k+ token contexts.
00:18:06 Daniel: long contexts amplify quantization artifacts and memory layout differences. we recommend profiling on your long-context traces and often keep high-precision for attention and key/value operations. our suggested QProfile for long context is more conservative.
00:18:28 Priya: in the deck we included a "long-context mode" qprofile that disables aggressive MLP quantization and prioritizes fp8 on attention. performance tradeoff is higher cost but quality remains closer to baseline.
00:18:45 Aisha: do you have any real customer case studies on cost savings vs quality impact?
00:18:50 Samira: yes — one health-tech customer went from baseline to a mixed QProfile and saved 38% on token bill with <1% measured drop on targeted metrics after iterative tuning. we'll share the redacted case study.
00:19:06 Mark: i'm concerned about model drift — if we quantize a new version, will we need to re-run full evals?
00:19:12 Daniel: yes, model architecture/weight deltas require re-profiling. Optimize can automate re-profiling as part of CI steps when you push a model version.
00:19:30 Miguel: quick note — kernel selection also depends on hardware. for example INT8 perf on A100 vs H100 differs; we store per-hardware profilers. for FP8 it's currently best on H100-like stacks, but our runtime supports emulation on other GPUs with performance penalties.
00:19:58 Natalie: H100 is on our roadmap; want to know exact perf numbers for our target fleet.
00:20:05 Daniel: we'll run the perf-runner on your fleet config. that's part of the POC.
00:20:15 (screen shows spreadsheet)
00:20:30 Priya: here's the quality vs latency waterfall for a tuned mixed profile: first we enable batching and prefix caching — big wins; then we enable mixed FP8 for attention — small drop in latency, negligible quality impact; finally INT8 global gives largest latency wins but we keep safety layers at FP8.
00:21:05 Mark: how many iterations does it usually take to find an acceptable qprofile?
00:21:10 Priya: it varies — usually 2–4 iterations with targeted prompt tests and one small canary in production.
00:21:25 Liam: about integration — do we need to change model hosting or just push q-blobs to the same inference endpoint?
00:21:32 Daniel: q-blobs are model artifacts — you register them as a new model variant in the catalog and route to it. no code change required in your application. you can pin to model variant via API.
00:21:50 Aisha: any estimate on the storage footprint increase for q-blobs?
00:21:55 Miguel: INT8 blobs are usually ~0.25–0.35x model size compared to fp32; fp8 sits in between. however, we keep both baseline and q-blob for safe rollback which increases storage needs during transition.
00:22:18 Mark: let's touch on pricing — if we reduce tokens by 30% with mixed profiles, will Redwood change billing mechanics?
00:22:26 Samira: billing is unchanged — tokens are tokens. the net effect is lower bill due to fewer tokens consumed or less GPU time. for Dedicated Reserved pricing we can model expected savings in SOW.
00:22:45 Natalie: we also need to ensure audits capture who applied a qprofile — need RBAC tie-in.
00:22:51 Miguel: audit logs include actor, timestamp, qprofile diff, and route scope. RBAC integrates via SAML/SOAML (sic) — (Samira: SAML) — sorry.
00:23:08 (laughter)
00:23:20 Mark: let's open the floor for a few technical questions. first, on numerical drift detection — any automated slack alerts?
00:23:30 Daniel: Optimize can push metrics to your monitoring — Datadog/Prometheus/Splunk. we ship delta metrics (rouge drop, perplexity changes) and you can set alerts.
00:23:50 Aisha: what about per-user personalization models — will quantization harm personalization embeddings?
00:23:58 Priya: embeddings are handled separately — Optimize has a parallel flow for embedding quantization which is conservative; we generally advise keeping user embeddings at higher precision or using post-hoc compression techniques.
00:24:20 Liam: can we walk through the POC scope briefly?
00:24:25 Samira: proposed POC scope: run baseline on your fleet, run 2–3 QProfiles (int8-fast, fp8-balanced, mixed-attn), evaluate on 5k prompts + 100k token trace, run a small canary in staging, deliver recommendations and SOW for production rollout. timeline: kickoff this week, benchmarking by 10/8, canary 10/15.
00:24:55 Mark: sounds good.
00:25:00 Natalie: data handling during POC — who gets access to the prompts and logs?
00:25:06 Miguel: access is shared via your drive; Redwood will only access prompts within the POC scope and we can sign a narrow data-processing addendum if needed.
00:25:20 (questions and clarifications continue)
00:30:05 Priya: a few gotchas from field: 1) watch out for tokenizers — quantization sometimes amplifies tokenizer edge cases; 2) check top-k sampling differences; 3) watch sequence-splitting logic for long contexts.
00:31:10 Aisha: about sampling — did you see changes to response diversity?
00:31:16 Priya: slight shifts in token probabilities mean diversity metrics like Dist-1 can drift; we encourage using nucleus sampling thresholds in tandem with QProfile testing.
00:32:00 Mark: any notes on retraining vs quantization — do you recommend fine-tuning after quantization?
00:32:07 Daniel: post-quantization fine-tuning (quant-aware training) sometimes recovers quality. Redwood doesn't train for customers by default, but you can perform QAT in your training pipeline before producing q-blobs; we support the q-blob format.
00:32:36 Aisha: ok. wrapping toward next steps — we need the perf scripts and the benchmark sheet.
00:32:44 Samira: i'll share those right after the call.
00:32:50 Mark: final question — what are common surprises customers hit in first week of canary?
00:32:55 Miguel: top surprises: 1) hallucination in a small subset — usually fixed by per-layer fp8 overrides; 2) mis-measured latency due to inadequate warm cache — warm the KV cache; 3) storage spikes if baseline q-blob retained for rollback — plan storage.
00:33:28 (brief silence)
00:33:40 Samira: ok, quick recap — Redwood to share perf-runner, benchmark spreadsheet, SOC2 & KMS guide; customer to share prompts and trace; SE to run mixed-batch benchmark and propose canary config. agreed next call for scoping on 2025-10-09.
00:34:05 Mark: agreed. thanks everyone.
00:34:12 Aisha: thanks, bye.
00:34:15 (call ends)

Meeting notes / quick artifacts:
